speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you've been experiencing the nosebleeds and spotting on your skin, and have you noticed any unusual bruising or bleeding from your gums?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any recent viral illnesses, fevers, or significant weight loss in the past few weeks? Also, is there any family history of bleeding disorders or similar symptoms in other relatives?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you observed any joint swelling, bone pain, or unusual fatigue in the child? I would also like to know if there have been any recent exposures to chemicals or new medications.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any information regarding the child's complete blood count, specifically the platelet count and white blood cell differential? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count, I suspect a platelet function disorder like Glanzmann thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome rather than a quantity issue. REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Function_Assay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of GIIb/IIIa receptors on the platelet surface is diagnostic for Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
